extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 named entity data
extraction.description: The CoNLL-2003 named entity data consists of eight files covering two languages, English and German, with a training file, development file, test file, and a large file with unannotated data for each language. The dataset is for language-independent named entity recognition and contains manually annotated named entities of four types: persons, organizations, locations, and miscellaneous names.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang; Fien De Meulder
extraction.citeAs: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder. 2003. Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled from existing text corpora: the English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus, and the German data was extracted from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau. For each language, training, development, test, and unannotated raw-data files were selected from these sources.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English source data were Reuters news stories from the Reuters Corpus. German source data were texts from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau. The dataset also included large unannotated raw-data files.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English: August 1996 to December 1996; German: August 1992 to December 1992
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp; mostly MUC conventions were followed, with an extra named entity category called MISC added.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The MISC category is very diverse because it includes names not in the other categories, including adjectives and events; The annotation assumes named entities are non-recursive and non-overlapping; when a named entity is embedded in another named entity, usually only the top level entity has been annotated.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The data consists of Reuters news stories in English and articles from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau, annotated for names of persons, organizations, locations, and miscellaneous entities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: developing a named-entity recognition system that includes a machine learning component; training and evaluating language-independent named entity recognition systems for English and German; incorporating unannotated data in the learning process
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was split into training, development, test, and large unannotated files for each language; additionally, for evaluation significance estimation, 250 random bootstrap resamples of sentences were drawn from each system output, and the organizers also converted system outputs to the same IOB tagging representation and searched for optimal majority-vote combinations of systems.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker were applied to the raw data. We created two basic language-specific tokenizers for this shared task. The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger. The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger.
